title: What should Doubt become?
question: Is repository-to-launch-artifacts the strongest path to a 5,000-star open-source project?
verdict: Do not ship LaunchKit as a standalone product. Keep launch artifacts as a distribution module and make source-grounded decision maps Doubt's core.

nodes.label: Current decision
nodes.text: LaunchKit is visually compelling but not a sufficiently open standalone wedge.

nodes.label: Distribution advantage
nodes.text: Launch artifacts create a built-in public distribution loop.

nodes.label: Commercial validation
nodes.text: RepoClip already turns a GitHub URL into narrated demo videos and reports hundreds of generated videos.

nodes.label: Open-source adjacency
nodes.text: OpenMontage includes a dedicated Screen Demo pipeline for product demos and documentation.

nodes.label: Local falsification
nodes.text: The deterministic LaunchKit probe produced a useful artifact for two repositories but generic filler for the repository without usable product metadata.

nodes.label: Market pull
nodes.text: Concrete creative and diagram agent workflows can attract a large GitHub audience.

nodes.label: Alternative wedge
nodes.text: A local-first evidence map has a clearer open-source window than a generic repo-to-video generator.

nodes.label: Demand signal
nodes.text: Causalith maps scientific research by claims and links compatible or conflicting statements to exact source spans.

nodes.label: Competition warning
nodes.text: Rigor already offers collaborative argument maps with AI verification, but describes a milestone-based path toward open sourcing rather than a fully open core today.

nodes.label: Missing evidence
nodes.text: No domain-reader preference test has yet shown that the map beats a well-cited research memo.

edges.note: A natural distribution loop argues for keeping the module.
Direct commercial competition narrows the open-source wedge.
A broad open-source video system already includes this workflow.
The no-model version failed one of three unfamiliar repositories.
The category can travel when it produces a finished public artifact.
Claim-level mapping is an active product need.
The product shape is not uncontested.
The decisive usability test remains undone.
It offers the most coherent next product for the Doubt brand.

sources.title: I Built an AI That Turns GitHub Repos into Demo Videos
sources.excerpt: RepoClip reads a GitHub repository and generates a professional demo video with narration, visuals, and music; the builder reports hundreds of generated videos.

sources.title: OpenMontage
sources.excerpt: The project lists Screen Demo as a pipeline for polished software screen recordings and walkthroughs used in product demos, tutorials, and documentation.

sources.title: LaunchKit probe result
sources.excerpt: With no README and no package description, the generated artifact fell back to generic claims and could not explain what the repository actually does.

sources.title: Causalith — Map research by claims, not citations
sources.excerpt: Causalith says it extracts claims with exact source spans and links papers that make compatible or conflicting claims, including papers that do not cite each other.

sources.title: Rigor — Structured Argumentation Platform
sources.locator: Homepage FAQ: What does the open source threshold mean?
sources.excerpt: Rigor maps claims, evidence, and rebuttals as interactive graphs and describes progressive open-source releases tied to usage and contribution milestones.
